short: The first pitched battle of the First English Civil War, ending in an indecisive stalemate that prolonged the conflict.
full:
On 23 October 1642, the armies of King Charles I and Parliament clashed at Edgehill in southern Warwickshire. Charles was marching on London to reclaim his capital, while a Parliamentarian force under the Earl of Essex moved to intercept him. Around 30,000 men fought in the engagement, which featured sweeping Royalist cavalry charges led by Prince Rupert that routed the Parliamentarian horse but disastrously chased them off the battlefield.

With the Royalist cavalry absent, Parliamentarian infantry counter-attacked and inflicted heavy losses on the king's center. Both sides fought to exhaustion until nightfall ended the carnage, leaving around 1,500 men dead. The inconclusive result meant that neither side could strike a knockout blow, guaranteeing that the civil war would be long, costly, and attritional.
